author: John Wagner
title: Redbirds hope to take steps towards state berth - NewsBreak
text:
By John Wagner ,
12 hours ago
Isanti Redbirds manager Steve Allen said preparing his team for a Town Ball season is a five-step process.
“The first step is to play a tough non-league schedule — and we came out of that pretty well,” he explained. “The second step is to survive the first month with all of the commotion, things like graduations and teams adding and subtracting players. You don’t always know who you’ve got.
“So you are trying to figure out who is available, and who will be able to help you. And we’ve handled that pretty well, too.”
Indeed the Redbirds have, as they come out of the Fourth of July break with a 9-3 season record that includes a 6-0 mark that’s good for the top spot in the Eastern Minny League’s South Division.
But Allen cautions that the third step may be the most difficult and important step of all.
“You are trying to figure out what this year’s team is going to be,” he said. “We should know that by the end of the month.
“We’ve got eight league games against tough teams. We’ll show our true colors in the next month or so.”
So far the team’s pitching has been solid. Phil Bray is 5-1 with a 0.55 ERA in 49 innings; James Green is 2-1 with a 3.86 ERA in four starts; and Ethan Smith is 2-0 with a 0.48 ERA.
“Our pitching has been thin because Tommy Heifort had arm surgery, and we haven’t had Matt Duong because of his Achilles injury,” Allen said. “So we have really leaned on those three guys.”
Offensively Troy Jones leads the regulars with a .375 batting average; Green leads the team in runs scored (16) while amassing 11 RBIs; and Smith is batting .368 with a team best 12 RBIs and eight runs scored.
Allen also said the Redbirds have performed well thanks in large part to veteran leadership shown by a number of different players. Among the veterans on the roster are Bud Heifort, Packy Lind, Jones, Green, Smith, and Bray.
“Our veterans know how to play the game — and they model that to our younger players,” Allen said. “
The fourth and fifth steps are pretty clear: The fourth is to perform well enough at the region tournament to be able to take the fifth and final step, and play in the Class B state tournament.
“The third step is important because if you do well, you will be set up for success at the region tournament,” Allen said, then added that his biggest concern heading into the season’s home stretch is to build a pitching rotation for July.
“Phil is on vacation for two weeks in July, so we’re trying to figure out how to hold everything together,” Allen said. “We’ll get Matt Duong back, and that will help. But we’re patching that together.”
Allen said he is confident his team will be able to take those final steps towards success.
“When we have everyone there, I feel we can play with anybody,” he said. “We still have to hit, but we’ve seen improvement in that area. We’re getting better at doing the little things like moving runners along, but we need to collect key hits with runners in scoring position.
“And if we can play solid defense, I think we have as good a chance as anybody.”
